Nous recherchons un Responsable Qualité Projet pour l’entité Hydroélectrique Amérique du Nord de GE Vernova. Dans ce rôle, le responsable qualité projet est le premier point de contact et la référence en matière de gestion de la qualité au sein d’une équipe projet. Il/elle assure le respect de toutes les exigences du processus de gestion de projet et des normes de GE Vernova. Il/elle favorise l’assurance qualité dans tous les domaines d’exécution et fonctions et s’assure du respect des engagements contractuels envers nos clients. 
 Job Description 
 Principales responsabilités
 Analyser et fournir les exigences du contrat relatives à la qualité à l'équipe de projet et soutenir les réunions de lancement des fonctions pour garantir que toutes les exigences spécifiques au contrat sont transmises à toutes les parties prenantes.
 Consolider les leçons apprises des projets précédents afin de les rendre exploitables pour prévenir les problèmes. Définir avec le directeur de projet la stratégie d'assurance qualité et d'identification des risques du projet.
 Produire le plan qualité du projet et les plans d’inspection et d’essai en collaboration avec les autres fonctions. Communiquer et s’assurer de l'application par les membres de l’équipe projet.
 Préparer et coordonner les inspections de qualité avec le client et de la chaîne d'approvisionnement conformément au plan d’inspection et d’essai.
 Gérer la préparation et la livraison du recueil de dossiers qualité des composantes avant livraison en garantissant la conformité aux exigences du client.
 Surveiller périodiquement les performances des processus du projet (Couts de non-qualité, non-conformités produits, livraison en temps, satisfaction client)
 Coordonner les enquêtes de satisfaction client en veillant à ce que nous recevions des réponses périodiques du client et à les traiter en conséquence.
 Gérer les rapports de non-conformité.
 Supporter le Directeur de Projet pour l'analyse et la gestion des coûts de non-qualité, le processus de réclamation associé, les actions curatives et de confinement, correctives et préventives associées.
 Soutenir l’équipe chantier pour la préparation de la documentation qualité et s’assurer que le contrôle qualité est fait conformément aux exigences du client.

 Baccalauréat d'une université ou d'un collège accrédité en génie avec un minimum de 5 ans d'expérience pertinente
 Bonne connaissance des principes et outils de gestion de la qualité
 Expérience pertinente en gestion de projets.
 Expérience en gestion de la relation client.
 Maîtrise de l'anglais et du Français
 Capacité à voyager occasionnellement au Canada et en Amérique du Nord.
 Qualifications /caractéristiques souhaitées :
 Expérience dans l'industrie hydroélectrique.
 Membre d'un permis d'exercice d'une profession canadienne d'ingénieur
 Certification en gestion de projet
 Leadership, proactivité, sens de l'urgence, autonomie ; capacité d'interagir avec les fonctions.
 Solides compétences en matière d'analyse et de pensée critique ; Solides compétences en communication.
 Gérer une activité multitâche dans un environnement multiculturel et global.
 Un état d'esprit d'amélioration continue.
 Job Description Summary 
 We are looking for a Project Quality Leader for GE Vernova's North American Hydroelectric entity. In this role, the Project Quality Leader is the first point of contact and the reference for quality management within a project team. He/she ensures compliance with all requirements of the project management process and GE Vernova standards. He/she promotes quality assurance in all areas of execution and functions and ensures compliance with contractual commitments to our clients. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Analyze and provide contract requirements related to quality to the project team and support function kickoff meetings to ensure that all contract-specific requirements are conveyed to all stakeholders. 
 Consolidate lessons learned from previous projects to make them actionable to prevent problems. Define with the project director the quality assurance strategy and identification of the project's risks. 
 Produce the project quality plan and inspection and test plans in collaboration with the other functions. Communicate and ensure the application by the members of the project team. 
 Prepare and coordinate quality inspections with the customer and supply chain in accordance with the inspection and testing plan. 
 Manage the preparation and delivery of the quality databooks for the components before delivery, ensuring compliance with the client's requirements. 
 Periodically monitor the performance of project processes (non-quality costs, product non-conformities, on-time delivery, customer satisfaction) 
 Coordinate customer satisfaction surveys ensuring that we receive periodic responses from the customer and process them accordingly. 
 Manage non-conformity reports. 
 Support the Project Director for the analysis and management of cost of non-quality, the associated claims process, the associated curative and containment, corrective and preventive actions. 
 Support the site team in the preparation of quality documentation and ensure that quality control is done in accordance with the client's requirements. 
 Required qualifications: 
 Bachelor's degree from an accredited university or college in engineering with a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience 
 Good knowledge of quality management principles and tools 
 Relevant experience in project management. 
 Experience in customer relationship management. 
 Fluent in English and French 
 Ability to travel occasionally within Canada and North America. 
 Desired Qualifications/Characteristics: 
 Experience in the hydropower industry. 
 Holder of a professional engineering license in Canada 
 Project Management Certification 
 Leadership, proactivity, sense of urgency, autonomy; ability to interact with functions. 
 Strong analytical and critical thinking skills; Strong communication skills. 
 Manage multitasking in a multicultural and global environment. 
 A mindset of continuous improvement. 
 Additional Information 
 Relocation Assistance Provided: No

 Minimum 5 years of experience operating mobile cranes.

 Thorough understanding of crane load charts, lift planning, rigging practices, and safe lifting procedures. 
 Strong mechanical aptitude with the ability to perform basic equipment inspections and routine maintenance.

 - Deliver Virtual Care with Impact: Review patient-submitted medical histories through our intelligent, graded online platform and determine candidacy for treatment. Most consultations take under 5 minutes to complete.

Our current focus includes health conditions such as:

 - Erectile dysfunction

 - Hair loss

 - Weight loss

 - Premature ejaculation

 - Testosterone therapy




WHO YOU ARE

 - Bilingual in French and English

 - Registered in good standing with the Ordre des infirmières et infirmiers du Québec (OIIQ), with eligibility for licensure in additional Canadian provinces (support available for the licensing process if needed)

 - Technologically savvy with experience or comfort in digital care platforms.

 - Excellent communicator who thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.

 - Able to respond to patient needs in a timely and empathetic manner.

 - Passionate about improving the Canadian healthcare landscape.

 - Curious, innovative, and excited to work cross-functionally with non-clinical teams.

 - Previous experience in men’s health is a plus, but not required.

 - Flexible Clinical Work: Patients are privately billed, no insurance paperwork or complex billing systems. The asynchronous nature of our platform means no live appointments with patients via video or phone call.

 - Seamless Technology: Our asynchronous platform was built by engineers who deeply understand provider pain points. It’s designed to support, not slow you down.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



Device Infrastructure Services owns the full lifecycle of hardware and operating systems across 1Password. The team is looking for the Staff Engineer who will lead its next chapter: a deliberate shift from legacy device management patterns towards devops and AI-enabled operations.



You'll be the technical leader of this team, responsible for setting the roadmap for this transformation and making sure it gets executed. This isn't a role where you hand off a roadmap and step back: you'll be in the build alongside the team, coaching engineers and raising the ceiling on what they're capable of. If you're excited by building scalable systems, shaping the strategy behind tools the whole company depends on, and bringing out the best work in the people around you, we want to hear from you.





How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.



What we're looking for:

 - 7+ years of IT and enterprise endpoint management experience, including 2+ years at a senior or staff IC level, with a track record of building and managing endpoints with Gitops practices.

 - Demonstrate broad knowledge of enterprise endpoint management, deep operating system-level experience, and the ability to recognize patterns across a fleet and build fixes that prevent recurrence.

 - Practical experience using AI tools to enable or accelerate IT operations and the judgment to know where AI speeds things up versus where it introduces risk.

 - Proven ability to define and drive technical roadmaps, seeing around corners and balancing long-term vision with near-term execution.

 -  Strong scripting and IaC ability (Bash, Python, and Terraform at minimum) — both writing production-quality automation yourself and reviewing others' code with a critical eye.

 -  Deep working knowledge of enterprise security fundamentals as they apply to endpoints: encryption, patch/vulnerability management, EDR, least-privilege enforcement, and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar).

 - Lead through change, collaborate effectively, and mentor engineers while maintaining a focused and impactful team environment.





What you can expect:

 - Own the technical direction of our Device Infrastructure Services, the tooling and standards that keep ~2,000 endpoints compliant, configured, and secure.

 - Drive the technical direction of a DevOps operating model for the fleet — config-as-code, version control, code review, and CI/CD pipelines in place of manual console changes — and drive adoption of that model across the IT team.

 -  Lead the adoption of responsible agentic AI across the device team, building the guardrails that decide what agents can act on autonomously and what still needs a human checkpoint.

 -  Act as the final escalation point for high-severity endpoint incidents, including deep machine-level diagnosis on both macOS and Windows hardware.

 - Partner across IT, Security, and product teams building custom solutions and helping push their initiatives across the finish line.

 - Assess and pilot new tooling (e.g., MDM platform migrations, patch management systems) and drive build-vs-buy decisions.

 - Collaborate with product teams to advise on features from the perspective of a real-world enterprise device deployment, and lead Customer Zero initiatives — piloting and stress-testing our own product against our internal fleet before it reaches customers.



What success looks like:

 - Establishing a clear 12-month roadmap for the transition to a GitOps-based operating model.

 - Building device health metrics and remediation standards for machine security, performance, and employee experience.

 - Developing our AI-assisted operations strategy, with automation milestones that balance speed, human review, security and agentic workflows.

 - Supporting the unpredictable release cadence of major OS vendors, and making sure those updates land safely across the org.

 - Bringing the team along with you — at 1Password, we Put People First. This role isn't just about leveling up what we can do technically, it's also about coaching the team along the way.

Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $122,000 CAD and $177,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.



This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

About Portless
 Portless is a dynamic and innovative 3PL provider revolutionizing how businesses manage their direct supply chain. We help merchants deliver a fast, reliable post-purchase experience through fulfillment and logistics built for cross-border scale, powered by international warehouses and global orchestration so they can grow with confidence.
 About the Role
 As Director (Head) of Customer Success Management, you own the post-launch merchant relationship for every Portless merchant and the team that delivers it. You lead the Customer Success Management motions, including onboarding & lifecycle teams.  You are the owner of Gross and Net Revenue Retention for the merchant base, and set the coverage model, playbooks, and cadences that turn the customer success flywheel (Adopt → Realize Value → Expand → Renew with Confidence) into a repeatable system across the Enterprise, Strategic, and Growth segments.
 This is a player-coach leadership role in a 0-to-1 environment. You will build the retention forecast leadership runs on, coach CSMs into commercially credible advisors, and partner with Technical Solutions, Operations, Product, Sales, and RevOps so that what we promise a merchant in a business review is what happens on the warehouse floor. You serve as an accountable partner in the success of our merchants and the Portless team members who support them.
 What You'll Own (Responsibilities)
 1. Team Leadership & Talent
 Build & Coach the Team: Hire, onboard, and develop CSMs & Hypercare managers (onboarding CSMs) across segments. Run weekly 1:1s, recorded call reviews (Gong), and a coaching cadence tied to a documented CSM competency model.
 Capacity & Book Design: Set book-of-business size and revenue coverage per CSM by segment, and re-balance books quarterly as merchants graduate from Hypercare or change tier.
 Performance Management: Define scorecards (retention, attach rate, health-score coverage, business review cadence) and hold the team to them with clear expectations and clear support.
 2. Retention, Forecasting & Risk Leadership
 Own GRR and NRR: Deliver Gross and Net Revenue Retention for the merchant base and publish a monthly retention forecast with named at-risk accounts, dollar exposure, and save plans.
 Risk Register Cadence: Run the weekly at-risk review. Every Yellow or Red account has a root cause, an owner, a dated next step, and an executive sponsor where needed.
 Churn Post-Mortems: Lead a written post-mortem within 10 business days of any logo loss or volume loss in the Enterprise and Strategic segments, and convert findings into playbook, operations, or product changes.
 Executive Escalations: Serve as the senior escalation point for Enterprise and Strategic merchants, driving root cause and corrective action across Operations, Technical Solutions, and Engineering.
 3. Coverage Model & Lifecycle Design
 Segmented Coverage: Design and run tiered engagement for Enterprise, Strategic, and Growth merchants, including a digital and pooled motion for the long tail so high-touch time goes where revenue and risk concentrate.
 Hypercare to CSM Graduation: Own the handoff standard from the four-phase Hypercare program (Stabilization → Enablement → Optimization → Graduation) into lifecycle CSM ownership, including handoff brief quality, a ≥90% graduation rate, and Peak Readiness: Lead merchant-facing peak planning (BFCM, Chinese New Year) with Operations: volume forecasts by merchant, inventory positioning, carrier mix, and surcharge communications delivered on a published calendar.
 4. Value Realization & Merchant Outcomes
 Health Scoring on Leading Indicators: Partner with CS Operations to design and maintain a merchant health score built on volume trend, exception rate, SLA attainment, stockout risk, invoice disputes, and engagement, and use it to trigger plays rather than to describe history.
 Executive Business Reviews: Set the standard for MBRs/QBRs/EBRs that quantify merchant outcomes in the merchant's terms (cost per order, delivery speed by country, cash flow released, exception rate) and end with agreed priorities and owners.
 Voice of the Merchant Program: Own the merchant sentiment system: risk scoring as the primary operating signal, Customer Effort Score at the transaction level, and decision-maker NPS as the relationship instrument, each with a defined response path and owner.
 5. Expansion via Services (Expand)
 Service Attach Rate: Own attach-rate targets and the expansion playbook for Portless services and partner solutions (Onward package protection, OpenBorder tax and duty compliance, Portless Capital inventory financing, US fulfillment expansion), with triggers, messaging, and objection handling documented for every play.
 Commercial Rigor: Coach CSMs on services-led discovery and business cases with clear merchant ROI. Partner with Sales on commercial terms and pipeline hygiene so influenced expansion is tracked in HubSpot, not in memory.
 Share-of-Wallet Growth: Identify merchants shipping a portion of their volume elsewhere and build the win-back and expansion motion with Sales and Operations.
 6. Systems, Data & Cross-Functional Leadership
 HubSpot as System of Record: Set and enforce data standards (health, phase, renewal, and expansion fields) so forecasts and dashboards can be trusted without manual reconciliation.
 AI-Assisted CS Operations: Deploy AI tooling where it removes CSM toil (call summaries, business review prep, anomaly alerts on volume and exceptions, draft merchant communications) and set the quality bar for when a human must review before anything reaches a merchant.
 Product & Operations Feedback Loop: Convert recurring merchant friction into ranked, evidenced requests to Product and Operations, and close the loop back to merchants when changes ship.
 Cross-Functional Accountability: Partner with the Head of Technical Solutions on implementation handoffs, with Account Champions in the China and Chicago FCs on Tier 1 and Tier 2 execution, and with RevOps on CS Ops tooling and reporting.
 Success Metrics (What "Good" Looks Like)
 Retention: Gross Revenue Retention at or above 90%, logo churn below 95%, and retention forecast accuracy within 10% points of actual.
 Growth: Net Revenue Retention above 100%, service attach rate of 15%, and influenced expansion pipeline and closed-won revenue tracked in HubSpot.
 Lifecycle: ≥90% Hypercare graduation rate, Sentiment: Decision-maker NPS at or above 50 (in collaboration with all of Portless leadership), with every detractor contacted within 5 business days.
 Team: New CSMs carrying a full book within 90 days, voluntary CSM attrition below 10%, and a documented competency model with quarterly calibration.
 Qualifications
 Fluent in English: Executive-level written and spoken communication. Able to run a board-ready retention review and a difficult merchant conversation in the same day.
 8+ Years in Customer Success or Account Management: Including 3+ years directly managing CSMs or Account Managers with ownership of retention and expansion targets.
 Domain Expertise: Fulfillment, 3PL, cross-border logistics, or e-commerce operations experience is required. You understand SLA attainment, exception rates, carrier mix, inventory positioning, duties and de minimis exposure, and why merchants leave a 3PL.
 Modern CS Operating Model: Hands-on experience designing segmented coverage models, leading-indicator health scores, retention forecasting, digital and pooled CS motions, and outcome-based business reviews.
 Commercial Rigor: Track record of services-led expansion, attach-rate management, and forecasting NRR alongside GRR.
 Analytical Depth: Comfortable in HubSpot, a BI tool (Metabase or equivalent), and spreadsheets. SQL is a strong plus. You interrogate the data yourself before you ask an analyst.
 AI Fluency: Has deployed AI tooling in a CS team (call intelligence, drafting, anomaly detection) and can articulate where it helped, where it failed, and what guardrails it needed.
 Platform Familiarity: Shopify ecosystem knowledge, plus experience with Intercom, Jira, and Gong or similar call intelligence tools.
 Values & Ways of Working
 Extreme Ownership: You own the retention number and every merchant escalation that reaches you, with a kind-and-caring orientation toward your team and the FC teams who execute.
 Judgment & Precision: Knows when to be strategically bold with a merchant's growth plan and when to be operationally precise about what Portless can deliver this week.
 Scalability: Builds playbooks, cadences, and coverage models that work for 100 merchants, and refuses one-off heroics as a growth strategy.
 Ideal Candidate Profile
 You have led CSM teams through a retention turnaround or a scale-up and can show the before-and-after numbers. You have worked inside fulfillment or e-commerce and know that a QBR slide about delivery speed means nothing if the carrier mix is wrong on Tuesday. You forecast churn with the discipline of a sales leader and coach with the patience of a great manager. You want to build the Customer Success Management function at a global 3PL from an early stage and be measured on Gross Revenue Retention, Net Revenue Retention, and the caliber of the team you build.

 Job Description 
 Key Responsibilities   
 • Plan, lead, and execute GMP audits across global operations and external partners.   
 • Assess compliance with regulations, quality standards, procedures, and guidance documents.   
 • Document audit observations, prepare reports, and communicate findings to stakeholders.   
 • Review and approve corrective and preventive action plans addressing audit findings.   
 • Provide expert guidance and training on audit activities .   
 • Escalate critical compliance issues and support timely mitigation activities when required .   
 • Maintain expertise in evolving regulations, industry standards, and quality expectations.

 • Degree in Chemistry, Pharmacy, Biology, Engineering, or another related scientific discipline; other degrees with relevant experience may be considered .

 COMPANY SNAPSHOT & MISSION

 BOLD: We take risks and stand for what we believe in.
 HONEST: We do the right thing and tell the truth when no one's watching.
 FINISHERS: We finish what we started.

 1% improvement every day. Set aside time to make impactful, long-term improvements and carefully document all processes within your department.
 AI-powered efficiency. Leverage AI tools to streamline workflows, gather insights, and generate data-driven recommendations.
 Process improvement & documentation. Identify operational or administrative bottlenecks and propose creative, tech-forward solutions. Document everything diligently to create the ultimate Tribe Support playbook.
 Culture advocate. Model WiFi Tribe’s values in everything you do.
 GROWTH & DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES
 Startup Exposure: Work closely with the executive team, gaining direct insights into scaling a global community and running a startup company.
 Increasing Responsibility: Possible opportunities to step into additional roles or tackle special projects aligned with your skill set.

 Strong organisational skills

 Strategic doer applying critical thinking to all tasks
 Autonomous (you'll be super successful with zero management)
 High integrity

 HOW TO APPLY / NEXT STEPS

 Initial Screening: A few assessments and a personality test to understand how you work.
 Video Questions: A few short video questions to learn more about your background, motivations, and personal interests.
 Main Interviews: A deeper discussion about your technical skills, personal-task management approach, and fit with our culture.
 Real-World Task Exercise: A short exercise simulating tasks you’d handle in this role.

 COMPENSATION

 PERKS

 Global Community: Engage with 700+ remote-working entrepreneurs and professionals and build your personal global network.
 Free Travel Opportunities: Join some of our WiFi Tribe Chapters for free (when last-minute spots are available) and experience travel adventures in some of the world’s most iconic destinations.
 Professional Development: We invest in our team through sponsored learning resources and conferences.
 Flexible Work: Balance personal and business tasks in a schedule that suits your style, as long as you're able to get everything done and respond on time.

 WiFi Tribe is built by people who care deeply, take bold action, and leave things better than they found them. If you’re a badass A-player ready to bring your talent, your heart, and your drive to a role that actually changes people’s lives, we’d love to meet you.
 Apply now — your next great adventure starts here.
